shouldFix.title: The edit falsifies file 08's '63 rows' and Decision 3's closed list of rewrites leaves it stale
shouldFix.finding: File 08's snapshot preamble reads: 'It exists because the register is meant to answer "where do we stand" without a reader reconstructing it from 63 rows.' Measured, that 63 is exact and composite: 12 inherited rows (DR-001..DR-012) + 30 V2 rows (DR-101..DR-130) + 5 five-review rows (DR-201..DR-205) + 16 DR-011 residual rows (R01..R16) = 63, with the 22 gate rows excluded. Inserting DR-131 and DR-133 makes it 65. Decision 3 enumerates exactly two sentences to rewrite and says 'Do not change conditions 1, 3, 4, or 5 measured cells'; the preamble is neither of the two, so a maintainer executing D-135 literally leaves a false number in the register. The entry never mentions the figure — '63 rows' and '65' both occur zero times in it. The register's two staleness escapes do not cover this: 'if this block and a row disagree, the row wins and this block is stale' governs disagreement with a ROW's content, and the regeneration instruction that follows governs STATUS-TOKEN counts by leading label. A row total is neither. I swept every numeric claim in file 08 — 1 of 11, 10 of 11, qualifying set = 11, 4 of 30, 5 of 5, 22 of 22, 18 of 18, 63 rows — and this is the only one the edit falsifies and the only one left unaddressed.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The figure is rhetorical rather than load-bearing; nothing computes from it, and no row status or readiness condition depends on it. The edit is still correct in everything it does specify.
shouldFix.repair: Name it as a third rewrite in Decision 3: replace '63 rows' with '65 rows', and state the composition (12 + 30 + 5 + 16, gates excluded) so the figure is re-derivable by the next act that adds a row. Alternatively, record expressly that the figure is left stale and why — but silence ships a false number in an authoritative file, which this corpus has repaired as a defect class repeatedly.

shouldFix.title: The new rows' source-pin cells cite coordinator decisions without file path or consent provenance, and their only file link points at a document the cell itself declares has no authority
shouldFix.finding: The register's own 'How to use the register' requires each row to name 'an owner or decision authority, exact source pin, required acceptance evidence, status, and blueprint impact'. Both proposed rows put 'D-132; D-134; recorded goal [file 12 §3](12-architecture-completion-goal.md) (file 12 has no authority)' in the source-pin column. Measured against the live table: 29 of the 30 existing V2 rows carry a file reference in that column, and the one that does not — DR-115 — still names `COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md` by path with its CONSENT digest. Every file-08 citation of a coordinator decision follows that form: DR-104 cites '`COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md` D-012 (CONSENT `e7b5c2b9…`)', DR-115 cites 'D-006 (three-turn adversarial consensus, CONSENT `bfd8a758…`)', and DR-130's ID cell cites 'D-010 … CONSENT `cd08c5f0…`'. The new rows cite bare 'D-132; D-134' with no file path, no CONSENT digest and no commit, and the only resolvable link in the cell points at file 12, which the same cell declares binds nothing. A reader following either new row's source column therefore lands on a no-authority document, while the two decisions that actually authorize the rows are named too loosely to pin.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 non-blocking advisory. Twenty attacks run, two landed.
